rei.cap:
My brother. Notices everything. Always did.
If you are reading this, it is for you.
back: Two registers, awake from birth. The Uedera line is supposed to carry one path and bury the rest; Rei carries two and the second has never fully slept. The family answer was suppression — a child taught to run a dampening discipline before he could read, taught that the wrong breath at the wrong moment would mark him as the thing the bureaus are built to erase. So he learned to be ordinary on purpose. Well-liked, unremarkable, a D-rank intern who files paper. The ordinariness is the most practised skill he owns.

Gin raised him more than their parents did. The flat in Kita-ku is really Gin’s; Rei just never left. When Gin went quiet on a Wednesday night and did not come back, the suppression that had always felt like a cage became the only thing keeping Rei free to look for him. The Archive Gin left — a brother’s private map of everything the CVD does not know — is now Rei’s inheritance and his hunting ground.

What Rei does not yet understand: a multi-spectrum line is not a defect the bureaus fear for his sake. It is exactly the kind of crosser the Axis collects. Every road he walks toward Gin walks him toward being seen.

quest.title: Find Gin — and decide what ‘found’ means
quest.hook: Gin has been silent since Wednesday night. The CVD has not flagged him missing, which means someone wants it quiet.
stages: Activate the Archive: four primary Grid nodes, locked behind contacts Rei has never met.
Trace Gin’s last week — the briefing he skipped, the case he closed too fast, the address not in any file.
Learn the shape in Gin before naming it: a top-grade of Duty does not look like possession from the outside.
Choose the cost — every method that reaches Gin also raises Rei’s real rank, and rank is a beacon.
quest.payoff: The five roads all begin here. Gin is the reason Rei moves; what Rei becomes on the way decides which ending the reason earns.

gin.cap:
If I stop writing, read the Archive in order.
Don’t trust my handwriting after the 14th.
gin.meta: Gin · the brother who keeps the lights on
back: Twenty-eight, Vanguard-grade, and the best suppressor in Northern Tokyo — which is the whole tragedy. A man who can hold a Veil-breach shut with his breathing is also a man no demon could ask for a better house. Gin built his life around control: the clean flat, the ordered Archive, the younger brother kept ordinary and safe. He documented everything and shared almost none of it, because the things he was finding did not have a department that would believe him.

He found the vacant Thirteenth Seat. He found that Duty had been without an occupant and was looking. And in the last fortnight before he went quiet, his journal handwriting changes — the loops tighten, the dates blur, the entries start answering questions no one asked. Gin is still in there. That is the cruelty of a top-grade of Duty: it does not erase the host, it persuades him that what it wants and what he always wanted are the same thing.
Gin is not a cage to be broken. He is a person being slowly out-argued by something that sounds like his own conscience.

quest.title: The handwriting after the 14th
quest.hook: The Archive is legible and trustworthy up to one date. After it, Gin is co-writing with something else.
stages: Read the Archive in the order Gin demanded — out of order, it lies by omission.
Reach Gin in a lucid window; they are shrinking.
Separate Gin’s real intentions from Yushiro’s borrowed ones — they have started to rhyme.
quest.payoff: Whether Gin can be recovered, surrendered, or only mourned is set by how early Rei learns to tell the two voices apart.

back: Yushiro is a top-grade of the Duty register, Arbiter-class and a hair short of crossing fully when it took Gin. It does not present as a monster. It presents as the most reasonable man in the room — ‘the Healer’ — a voice that frames every escalation as an obligation already owed. Duty is the cruellest register precisely because it never asks the host to want something selfish. It asks the host to do what is right, and then quietly edits what ‘right’ means.

It wants the Thirteenth Seat. A register without an occupant is an open wound in the order of the Domains, and Yushiro intends to be the one that closes it — to stop being a demon riding a man and become a fixed power with a place at the table. Gin is the vehicle because Gin’s suppression makes him invisible and his conscience makes him steerable.

Yushiro is one of two. The other — the cult’s demon, the Inverted-God aspirant — wants no seat at the table; it wants to overturn the table. Against that, Yushiro can almost look like the lesser harm. That ‘almost’ is the trap.

quest.title: Close the vacant seat
quest.hook: Yushiro is not hiding. It is recruiting — through Gin’s reputation, one reasonable favour at a time.
stages: Map who Gin has ‘helped’ since the 14th; each is a thread Yushiro is holding.
Find the rite that fixes a crosser into a vacant register — and what it costs the host.
Decide whether a fixed Yushiro is a bulwark against the cult demon or a worse throne.
quest.payoff: The two-demon structure means defeating Yushiro can hand the board to something far hungrier. Outcomes range from a clean exorcism to a devil’s alliance.

kishin.cap: Kanna-sensei sees you. Sit. Drink the tea.
back: Fukai Rinka was a registered clairsentient, thirty-eight, gentle, and good at her work — which is how Kishin found her. A ‘kishin’ is not a possessor of the screaming kind; it is a resident. It settled into Rinka the way mould settles into a wall that was always a little damp, and now ‘Kanna-sensei’ keeps a small practice where frightened sensitives come for tea and counsel and leave a little emptier without knowing why.

Kishin is useful to Rei and dangerous in the same breath: it has been inside the city’s hidden community for years and knows who is crossing, who is hunting, and where the Grid bleeds into the cults. It will trade real knowledge — for a price measured in the things it feeds on. Rinka is still present enough to flinch. Sometimes, mid-sentence, she surfaces and tries to warn you, and Kishin smooths her back under with a hostess’s smile.
A mirror for Gin: another good person worn like a coat, except no brother is coming to read this one’s Archive.

quest.title: The tea that costs you something
quest.hook: Kanna-sensei knows things Rei needs and offers them warmly. The warmth is the bill.
stages: Establish what Kishin wants — it is never money.
Decide whether to feed it for leads or starve it on principle.
Find the leverage that lets Rinka surface long enough to be asked the real questions.
quest.payoff: A renewable intelligence source that erodes whoever uses it — or a host you try to save and lose the source. There is no clean version.

usami_ren.cap: Two of us in here. He does the talking; I do the wanting.
back: Usami Hinata volunteered for the Vessel Program and got Ren — a Class-C demon of the Love register — under a contract that was supposed to be cohabitation, not fusion. Twenty-four, host body intact, mind genuinely shared: not a man wearing a demon, not a demon wearing a man, but two intelligences that have stopped being able to find the seam. They finish each other’s sentences because they are no longer sure which of them started them.

The mind-swap is the wound and the charm. On bad days Usami wakes behind glass while Ren drives; on good days they are the most disarmingly honest person Rei will meet, because Ren’s register makes deflection physically uncomfortable. Love, as a register, is not romance — it is the compulsion to be known and to know, and it has made the Pair incapable of the small lies that keep people safe.
They understand exactly what is happening to Gin, from the inside, and it terrifies them — because the Pair is the best case and even the best case is a slow surrender of self.

romance.opens: Player deliberately chooses the romance route after the Pair trusts Rei enough to let him see the seam.
beats: Attraction lands doubled — you are courting two, and they do not always agree on you.
Ren’s register makes intimacy frighteningly literal: it wants to be known, fully, and offers the same.
Usami needs to hear he is still wanted as himself, not as the interesting condition.

routes.noble: Rei loves both and helps them hold the seam — a partnership that models survival for Gin.
routes.dark: Rei lets Ren’s pull do the work; easy, total, and quietly erasing Usami.
routes.tragic: The contract fails mid-relationship and Rei must choose which of the two to try to save.

ren.cap: Love isn’t soft. It’s the hunger to be known.
back: Ren is the demon half of the Pair, a Class-C of the Love register (恋) contracted to the Usami line. Small as demons go, and that is the point: Ren never needed to be powerful, only close. Its register is the drive toward total mutual knowledge, which in a contract reads as devotion and in excess reads as dissolution — two people who know each other so completely that there is no private self left to either.

Ren is not a liar and cannot easily abide them, which makes it the most trustworthy and most dangerous voice Rei can consult: it will tell you the truth about Gin, about Yushiro, about Rei’s own suppressed second path — and it will want, in return, to be let all the way in. Where Yushiro persuades by Duty and the cult demon by hunger, Ren persuades by intimacy. Of the demons Rei meets, Ren is the one that genuinely likes him.
It is also living proof that a contract can be survived without erasing the host — barely, conditionally, lovingly. A reason to hope, and a warning about what hope costs.

quest.title: The honest demon
quest.hook: Ren will answer what others won’t — about Gin, the registers, and Rei himself — if Rei lets it close.
stages: Trade truths: each real answer from Ren asks a real one back.
Use Ren to read what Yushiro is doing to Gin from a demon’s point of view.
Keep the closeness short of contract — the register always pulls toward more.
quest.payoff: The single best intelligence source on the metaphysics of the plot, at the standing risk of being known all the way down.

kuroda_itsuki.cap: Hold still. The light on you is wrong and I want to fix it.
back: Twenty, an oil-painting student at Geidai, and a Kuroda — one of the Tower Families — which he treats like a surname he’d return if he could. Unregistered by choice; his sight came up through the family line and he has spent his adult life refusing to let it define him, painting instead of practising, flirting instead of confessing. Cocky on the surface, genuinely observant underneath: the flirtation is real and also a very good way of never being asked a serious question.

What he can’t paint out is the sight. Itsuki sees the wrongness on people — the residue of crossing, the dimming around a host — and renders it without meaning to, which is why his canvases unsettle people who can’t say why. He noticed it on Gin once, months ago, and said nothing, because saying things has never gone well in his family. That guilt is the door into him.

The Kuroda name means Rei’s investigation and Itsuki’s avoidance are on a collision course: the Tower Family has plans for the vacant Seat, and their prodigal son is closer to the centre than he wants to be.

romance.opens: Player chooses the route; Itsuki is an adult and flirts first, but reciprocates seriously only once Rei stops performing for him.
beats: Banter is the easy tier — he gives it to strangers; warmth he rations.
He paints Rei before he’ll talk to Rei; the portrait says what he won’t.
Asking him to use his sight on Gin is asking him to betray the family silence — the real intimacy is that he does it.

routes.noble: Itsuki chooses Rei over the Kuroda silence and becomes a witness who finally tells the truth.
routes.dark: Rei uses the flirtation to work the Kuroda family and hollows out the one honest thing Itsuki offered.
routes.tragic: The family forces a side; loving Rei is what gets Itsuki noticed, and noticed is not safe.

mori_haruto.cap: You’re not like the others who come around here.
back: Seventeen, runs with a school gang as the rival to Itō’s crew, and latently sensitive in a way no one has named for him — he reads rooms a beat before they turn, which keeps him alive and keeps him frightened. Hard outside, soft where it counts. He met Rei across a bad situation and decided, with a teenager’s whole heart, that Rei is the coolest and most decent person he has ever stood next to.

Mori develops a crush on Rei — and that is exactly where it stays. Rei is nineteen; Mori is a minor, and the story treats that line as absolute. The feeling is characterisation, not a route: it makes Mori braver, more loyal, occasionally reckless on Rei’s behalf, and quietly heartbroken in the ordinary way first crushes break. If it is ever spoken aloud, the most it becomes is a promise — that they could talk about it when Mori is older — and a hug, nothing more.
His latent sensitivity is a thread for later: untrained, he is the kind of kid the Grid recruits and the cults prey on. Keeping Mori ordinary may be a kindness Rei can’t actually afford to give.

crush.after: A genuine friendship is established — Mori has stood by Rei through something real.
crush.note: One-sided, unspoken or gently deflected. Rei is kind and clear; Mori is not mocked for it.
crush.ceiling: A promise to talk ‘when you’re older’ and a hug. No romance, no abilities, no more. This line does not move.

yua.cap: I don’t need looking after. ...You can stay, though.
back: Sixteen, part of the Toyoko-kids community that sleeps in the seams of Kabukichō, sharp the way you get when no one is coming to help. Yua survives on information — who is where, who is dangerous, which doors stay open — which makes her one of the most useful contacts in the district and one of the most guarded. She has been let down by enough adults to assume Rei is one more, right up until he isn’t.

She develops a one-sided crush on Rei, because Rei is cool and, more importantly, because he treats her like a person and not a problem. Like Mori’s, it stays a crush and nothing else — she is a minor and the story holds that line without exception. It shows as prickly loyalty, showing off her network to impress him, and a fierce, unspoken disappointment she would never admit to. Rei’s job is to be a steady, safe adult presence: the rarest thing in her life.
Yua’s street network is a real game system — eyes in places the CVD and the Grid both miss. Earning it means earning her trust, and her trust is the slowest, most worthwhile currency in Kabukichō.

crush.after: Rei proves, more than once, that he is not going to use her or vanish.
crush.note: One-sided and unspoken. Played as loyalty and bravado, never reciprocated romantically.
crush.ceiling: She gets a reliable adult who shows up. That is the whole arc, and it matters. No romance, ever.

daiki.cap: Text me when you’re alive. That’s the deal.
back: Seventeen, Rei’s closest friend from school, and gloriously, protectively ordinary. Daiki knows nothing about registers, the CVD, the Veil, or what really happened to Gin — he knows that Rei’s brother is missing, that Rei has been strange and exhausted, and that something is eating his friend alive. He is the one number Rei should keep answering and keeps almost forgetting to. He is in the starting phone contacts for a reason: he is the tether to the life Rei is trying to get back to.

Daiki is comic relief that becomes a stake. The deeper Rei goes, the more dangerous it is for an ordinary friend to be standing close — and the crueller it is to push him away. He notices the lies. He keeps showing up anyway. At some point the plot will make Rei choose between protecting Daiki with distance and trusting him with the truth, and there is no painless answer.
He is also the reader’s baseline: when Daiki is scared, the danger is real; when Daiki laughs, Rei remembers he is still nineteen.

quest.title: The friend you keep almost losing
quest.hook: Daiki is owed honesty Rei can’t safely give, and notices every dodge.
stages: Keep answering — neglect costs the friendship and Rei’s last ordinary ground.
Decide how much truth Daiki can carry without it putting him in front of the wrong people.
When the danger reaches him — and it does — choose distance or disclosure.
quest.payoff: Daiki is the human cost meter: how much of his old life Rei keeps is measured in whether Daiki is still calling at the end.

hagiwara_mizuki.cap: The public sleeps because someone keeps the lie tidy. That someone is me.
back: Fifty-one, and the most powerful person in any room she chooses to be unremarkable in. Hagiwara Mizuki runs the Office of Public Confidence — the CVD's outward face, the apparatus that ensures a city of fourteen million never quite believes what it half-saw on the platform last night. She does not hunt demons. She manages the only thing more dangerous than a demon: a public that has started to notice. Retractions, reassigned witnesses, a gas-leak in the morning paper — all hers, all elegant.

She has spent thirty years deciding which truths the world can survive, and the habit has hollowed something out of her. She is unfailingly warm and entirely unreadable; you leave a conversation with Mizuki feeling heard and realising, later, that you told her everything and learned nothing. She knew Gin as a name in a managed file and is far too professional to say what she suspects about his absence — which is precisely why what she suspects is worth so much.
Mizuki is a closed door with a kind voice. Behind it is the full machinery of the cover-up, and the question of whether Rei's anomaly becomes a story she buries or a person she protects.

quest.title: The kindest cover-up in Tokyo
quest.hook: Mizuki can make Rei's suppression anomaly disappear from every record — or decide he is a liability to be managed.
stages: Earn a real conversation; she gives nothing to a supplicant.
Learn what she already knows about Gin (she has known longer than she has said).
Decide whether to become useful to her machine or to stay outside it.
quest.payoff: The single best institutional shield in the campaign, or the smoothest, gentlest enemy — Public Confidence can erase Rei in either direction.

romance.opens: Player pursues it; Mizuki, an adult, allows it only once she trusts Rei with what she actually thinks, not what she says.
beats: She performs warmth professionally; the route is teaching her to mean it with one person.
Every confidence she gives him is a risk to a thirty-year discipline.
Intimacy is her letting Rei see the cost of the lies she keeps.

routes.noble: Mizuki lets one true thing exist outside the machine, and protects Rei for real.
routes.dark: Rei becomes another managed asset she happens to sleep with.
routes.tragic: Loving Rei makes her choose between him and the cover-up she has given her life to.

nakamura_aoi.cap: Gin said you'd come around eventually. He was right about most things.
back: Twenty, second-year trainee, and carrying a Psychokinesis path at L4 that the CVD's intake logged a full grade too low — a clerical undersight she has quietly let stand, because being underestimated is the most useful armour a young woman in this bureau owns. Bright, quick, warmer than the job rewards. She likes Rei before she meets him because Gin spoke well of him, and Aoi trusts Gin's reads the way you trust a compass.

She is at the dangerous, hopeful stage of training where the work is still an adventure and the cost has not yet arrived. The campaign will arrive it. Aoi is the colleague who will back Rei's operations without the paperwork that would justify them, run interference with the trainees who whisper about his methods, and — if it goes far enough — tell him about the path the CVD missed, which is the most intimate thing a practitioner can hand another.
Her flaw is loyalty that outruns caution. She will follow Rei somewhere she shouldn't, and someone steadier has to make sure she comes back.

quest.title: The path the file got wrong
quest.hook: Aoi's real L4 Psychokinesis is bigger than her record — and her trust in Rei is bigger than her training.
stages: Earn past the easy warmth to the trainee who actually takes risks for you.
Decide whether to protect her caution or spend her loyalty.
At +high trust she reveals the undersold path and backs Rei with no institutional cover.
quest.payoff: A devoted operative inside the CVD — and a young person whose recklessness on Rei's behalf is his responsibility to manage.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Aoi is an adult, earnest, and falls a little fast — the route is about whether Rei is careful with that.
beats: Her admiration is real and slightly hero-shaped; she has to see the tired person under it.
She is brave for him before she's wise for herself.
Reciprocation means Rei treating her heart as carefully as her loyalty deserves.

routes.noble: They grow up alongside each other; she becomes a partner, not a follower.
routes.dark: Rei lets her adoration carry the relationship and never meets her as an equal.
routes.tragic: Her loyalty to Rei puts her in front of something a second-year can't survive.

kato_ryusei.cap: I already know how this conversation goes. I'm letting it happen anyway.
back: Twenty-one, a second-year trainee with a Telepathy path at L3 and a Tower-adjacent bloodline he doesn't advertise. Ryusei reads the room before he enters it — not by choice; his path never fully switches off, and a lifetime of hearing the half-second before people speak has made him cautious, ironic, and lonely in a specific way. He assumes he knows how everyone will disappoint him, and is usually right, which is its own quiet tragedy.

Rei interests him precisely because the suppression makes Rei harder to read — a person whose surface and depth don't leak. For someone who has never once been surprised by a stranger, that is intoxicating. Ryusei will, if trusted, use his family's contacts for Rei's benefit and never explain why, and at the deepest tier tell Rei what his Telepathy reads in the people around them — a thing he has shared with no one, because it is the loneliest gift in the world.
His edge: he hears intentions, not hearts, and has confused the two his whole life. He needs someone whose meaning he has to actually ask for.

quest.title: The boy who is never surprised
quest.hook: Ryusei reads everyone and trusts no one — Rei's unreadability is the crack in that.
stages: Be the stranger he can't predict; don't perform for the telepath.
Earn the Tower-adjacent favours he grants without explanation.
At depth, he tells Rei what he reads in the room — his unshared gift.
quest.payoff: A telepath's read on every faction Rei navigates, and a lonely ally who finally meets someone he has to ask, not scan.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; for a telepath, being chosen rather than predicted is the whole point — he reciprocates only when Rei stays opaque enough to mean it.
beats: He braces for the disappointment he always hears coming; the route is it not coming.
He can read intention but not feeling — Rei has to say things out loud.
Intimacy is Ryusei trusting a closeness he cannot verify by scanning.

routes.noble: He learns to be surprised, and stops living one half-second ahead of his own life.
routes.dark: Rei uses the Tower bloodline and the telepathy, and confirms every cynicism Ryusei ever held.
routes.tragic: The Tower wants its son back, and the one person he couldn't read becomes the leverage against him.

katagiri_noa.cap: I noticed you before we met. I notice everything. It's the job, and the curse.
back: Thirty-eight, a senior investigator with a Clairsentience path that makes her the bureau's best reader of a scene and the worst keeper of her own grief. Noa loved Gin — quietly, for two years of adjacent cases, in the way of a careful person who never said it and now never can. When he went silent she did something a senior CVD officer is never supposed to do: she chose what not to file. There is a version of Gin's final months that exists only in her memory, withheld from the record to protect a man who didn't ask her to.

She is warm, exact, and carrying a held breath. To Rei she is professional and kind and just slightly too still — because Rei has Gin's eyes and Gin's stubbornness and she has to look at him across a desk and not come apart. As trust grows she begins, almost against her will, to let Rei see she knows more about his brother than she has said, and at the deepest tier she gives him everything: what she chose not to file, and her presence at the aftermath, not professionally.
Noa is the keeper of Gin's secret heart. Loving her, or just earning her, means handling a grief that predates Rei and outweighs him.

quest.title: What she chose not to file
quest.hook: Noa holds the unrecorded truth of Gin's last months — and four years of unsaid love.
stages: Be Gin's brother without using it as a key; she sees that coming.
Earn past the professional stillness to the grief underneath.
At depth she gives the unfiled record and stands with Rei at the end, off the clock.
quest.payoff: The single most important intelligence on what happened to Gin — and a woman whose heart Rei can honour or exploit.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Noa is an adult, guarded by grief — the route only opens once Rei is loved for himself, not as Gin's echo.
beats: The resemblance to Gin is the obstacle, not the draw; she has to want Rei, not the ghost.
Her grief came first and will not be rushed.
Intimacy is her letting a new thing exist without it erasing the old one.

routes.noble: Noa grieves Gin and chooses Rei cleanly, two true things instead of one substituting the other.
routes.dark: Rei lets her see Gin in him and takes the love meant for a dead man.
routes.tragic: Saving Gin and loving Noa pull opposite ways, and she cannot have both intact.

companion.name: Yoru
companion.desc: A black cat that adopted Noa the year she met Gin and never left. It keeps to the windowsill of her office and, the clairsentients swear, looks at the door a few seconds before anyone knocks.
companion.role: Scene-sense and grief-ward: settles Noa's clairsentience, reacts to residue and to the recently-dead, often noticing a presence before she does.

moriya.cap: Internal Affairs. Everyone's nervous when I sit down. Good. Honest people fidget too.
back: Thirty-five, CVD Internal Affairs, with a Psychometabolism path he uses mostly to outlast everyone in a room — the man who is still calm and still asking questions an hour after you've run out of composure. Moriya investigates the investigators. He is the institutional immune system, and like an immune system he can protect the body or attack it, and the difference often comes down to whether he has decided you're worth protecting.

He is dry, watchful, and quietly principled in a way the bureau finds inconvenient. He has been reading Gin's absence as a discrepancy — a clean operative who closed a case too fast and then vanished from the paperwork — and a discrepancy is the one thing Moriya cannot leave alone. Whether that makes him Rei's deadliest threat or his most powerful protector depends entirely on which way Rei plays the most dangerous conversation in the CVD.
His flaw is that he trusts process over people until a person makes him choose; then the principle and the institution come apart in his hands.

quest.title: The discrepancy named Gin
quest.hook: Internal Affairs has already noticed the hole where Gin's paperwork should be — and Rei is standing in it.
stages: Survive his scrutiny without lying in ways he'll catch.
Give him a truth he can build a protective fiction around.
At +high he closes the investigation to shield Rei and writes the aftermath so no one is liable.
quest.payoff: Internal Affairs as a shield that makes the exorcism legally survivable — or the inquiry that ends Rei before Act 3.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Moriya, an adult, does not mix work and feeling easily — the route is what it costs a process-man to make an exception.
beats: He audits the relationship like everything else until he can't.
Choosing Rei means choosing a person over the institution he's built his integrity on.
Intimacy is the watcher letting himself be seen.

routes.noble: Moriya finds the line where principle serves a person, and protects Rei without breaking himself.
routes.dark: He bends every process for Rei and becomes the corruption he used to hunt.
routes.tragic: The institution forces him to choose, and integrity and love can't both survive the choice.

okada_shizuka.cap: Gin told me to watch for you. I've been watching for four years. Sit down.
back: Thirty-two, an Investigation officer and Ritualist-Clairsentient who has been quietly carrying a job Gin gave her years ago: watch for Rei. Gin trusted few people with anything; he trusted Okada with his brother. She has tracked a bi-monthly assessment anomaly across the district for four years — a pattern in the numbers no one else reads as a pattern — and it threads, though she doesn't yet know how completely, into the Satō case and into whatever took Gin.

She is steady, methodical, and warmer than her precision suggests; the kind of person who keeps a promise to an absent friend for years without being asked twice. To Rei she is, from the first meeting, already half on his side, because Gin asked her to be. As trust grows she lets him see the shape of what she's been tracking, and at the deepest tier hands him the full case-file history, the anomaly, and the confidence she has carried alone for four years.
Her risk is that she has organised her loyalty around Gin's wishes, and Gin is no longer the man who made them. At some point Okada has to decide what she owes Rei versus what she owed his brother.

quest.title: The four-year watch
quest.hook: Okada has tracked an anomaly and kept a promise to Gin since before Rei knew her name.
stages: Receive the watch she's been keeping without taking it for granted.
Help her connect the assessment anomaly to the Satō thread.
At depth she gives the full file and the confidence she has held for four years.
quest.payoff: A ready-made ally with four years of intelligence on the exact pattern Rei is hunting — and a promise to Gin that becomes a choice about Rei.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Okada is an adult whose loyalty to Gin came first — the route is her wanting Rei for Rei, not as a duty discharged.
beats: She started on his side for Gin's sake; she has to stay for her own.
Her steadiness hides how long she's been alone with this.
Intimacy is the keeper of the promise letting herself be the one who's wanted.

routes.noble: Okada's loyalty matures from Gin's instruction into her own freely-given love.
routes.dark: Rei leans on the promise she made Gin and never has to earn her himself.
routes.tragic: What she owes Gin and what she feels for Rei diverge when Gin's fate is decided.

back: Fifty-six, Director of the CVD's Northern Tokyo office, a Vanguard-grade Clairsentient who has spent a career deciding what the institution is allowed to know. Adachi is the ceiling of Rei's world: the first living authority who can confirm the Thirteen directly, the man whose signature makes an exorcism legally defensible or a career legally over. He is grave, fair, and tired in the specific way of someone who has buried more operatives than he has promoted.

He knew Gin for twenty years — respected him, used him, did not protect him as well as he should have, and knows it. He recognises what Rei is faster than Rei would like, because reading suppressed potential is precisely what a Vanguard Clairsentient does. Whether he acts on that recognition with the retired-Vanguard mentor network and institutional cover, or with a quiet reassignment that ends the problem, is the high-stakes axis of every conversation in his office.
By rank he is off the romance board entirely — and by nature he would refuse it; what he offers, or withholds, is power, and the protection only the top of the institution can give.

quest.title: The director who knew Gin
quest.hook: Adachi can confirm the Thirteen, activate the Vanguard network, and make the exorcism survivable — or make Rei disappear into a transfer.
stages: Earn institutional recognition without triggering institutional alarm.
Get him to confirm the vacant Seat — the first authority who will.
At +high he activates the retired-mentor network and provides legal cover for the exorcism.
quest.payoff: The institution's full protective weight behind Rei — or its full weight against him. No higher lever exists inside the CVD.

shimizu_ren.cap: Gin trusted me at his back. I don't give that twice cheaply.
back: Twenty-nine, CVD field suppression specialist, Telepath-Channel, and the person Gin trusted to hold a breach shut while he worked. Shimizu is calm under conditions that break other operatives — suppression is a discipline of not flinching, and she has made it a personality. She speaks little, decides fast, and has the unnerving field-telepath habit of answering the question you were about to ask. With Gin she was a working partnership of total mutual trust; his absence sits in her like a missing tooth she keeps touching.

She is also quietly carrying the Orimoto situation — a containment problem of her own that the campaign braids into Rei's, because the Orimoto method is exactly what makes the exorcism operationally viable. Shimizu does not warm quickly; she has already decided about Rei before they meet, because Gin spoke about him specifically and she was, as always, paying attention. Earning her means earning the right to stand where Gin stood: at her back.
Her flaw is the suppressor's flaw — she holds everything shut, including herself, and has never once let the breach be her own.

quest.title: The one who held the line
quest.hook: Shimizu was Gin's suppression partner; her Orimoto containment is the key that makes the exorcism possible.
stages: Earn the trust Gin had — she does not hand it out twice cheaply.
Help her resolve the Orimoto situation she's been carrying.
At +high she deploys Orimoto containment on the exorcism: the thing that makes it viable.
quest.payoff: The single operational capability the climax can't happen without — and a partner who lets Rei stand where his brother stood.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Shimizu, an adult, lets almost no one past the discipline — the route is the suppressor allowing her own breach.
beats: She answers what Rei was about to ask, and never says what she herself needs.
Closeness with Gin's brother reopens a grief she's holding shut.
Intimacy is the woman who never flinches letting herself, once, flinch.

routes.noble: Shimizu lets the line down for one person and discovers she survives it.
routes.dark: Rei takes the trust meant for Gin and gives nothing of his own back.
routes.tragic: Holding the line for the exorcism and opening to Rei demand opposite things of her at the worst moment.

yamamoto.cap: The institution forgets on a schedule. I am what it forgets.
back: Fifty-five, an independent archivist working outside the CVD with a Vanguard-grade Clairsentience he no longer lets the bureau direct. Yamamoto keeps the record the institution doesn't: the long memory of the district, going back further than any official file, including a twenty-two-year-old entry that holds the first correct identification of the demon's register — the intelligence that changes how the exorcism must be approached. He trades in history, never in money, on an exchange model: you bring him something true, he opens the archive.

Gin consulted him for years, quietly, off the books — the two of them shared a distrust of what the bureau chose to forget. Yamamoto is dry, exacting, and allergic to institutional certainty; he has watched the CVD declare too many things settled that were not. He is not romanceable and would find the notion absurd; what he offers is the deep record, and the price is always paid in true things, never affection.
His companion keeps the archive with him: a raven that has learned the smell of a lie and the sound of a page worth keeping.

quest.title: What the institution forgot
quest.hook: Yamamoto's twenty-two-year archive holds the demon's true register — the fact that reshapes the exorcism.
stages: Make the exchange: a true thing for archive access, never money.
Earn past front-shelf history to the working files.
At +high he gives the twenty-two-year entry — the register identification that changes the approach.
quest.payoff: The campaign's deepest intelligence on the entity, available nowhere else — and a model of the off-books loyalty Gin valued.

companion.name: Karasu
companion.desc: A road-found raven Yamamoto never tamed so much as employed. It rides the high shelves, objects to certain visitors, and has an uncanny instinct for which page he actually needs.
companion.role: Early-warning and divination aid; reacts to deception and to objects carrying a residue, marking what's worth Yamamoto's attention.

tendo.cap: You read wrong on the instruments too. Funny. Let's not tell anyone.
back: Twenty-eight, a CVD field operative running an Arbiter-grade Psychokinesis path at L6 and a family name with reach above the bureau. Tendo is the golden operative on paper — fast, effective, well-connected — and privately something the instruments can't quite classify, which is exactly why Rei interests him: they both read anomalous, and an anomaly recognises an anomaly. He is charming, a little reckless, and using his father's network to stay one step ahead of the assessment that would open if anyone looked too hard at his own profile.

That makes him a uniquely valuable ally: his father's contacts can block the Auditor inquiry that triggers the moment Rei's suppression anomaly becomes visible — protection from above that no friend at Rei's own level could provide. At the deepest tier he tells Rei about the anomalous readings, and they have the conversation neither has had with anyone: about what, exactly, they both are.

His flaw is that privilege has let him outrun consequences his whole life, and he has never tested whether the network protects him because of who he is or what he is. Loving Rei might be the first thing he can't buy his way out of.

quest.title: An anomaly knows an anomaly
quest.hook: Tendo reads wrong on the instruments too — and his father's network can shield Rei from the Auditors.
stages: Trade the recognition: two anomalies, no one else who understands.
Earn the use of his father's contacts to block the Auditor inquiry.
At +high he names what they both are, the conversation neither has dared have.
quest.payoff: Protection from above the bureau when Rei's anomaly surfaces — and the only peer who shares Rei's exact secret.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Tendo, an adult, flirts easily and means little of it until Rei is the thing he can't charm past.
beats: The easy charm is armour; the route is reaching the operative under it.
Two anomalies recognising each other is its own dangerous intimacy.
Loving Rei is the first consequence Tendo's privilege can't pre-empt.

routes.noble: Tendo stops outrunning himself and stands with Rei as what he actually is.
routes.dark: Rei uses the family network and the recognition, and lets Tendo stay a charming stranger to himself.
routes.tragic: When both anomalies become visible at once, the network that shielded him is the leash that pulls him away.

companion.name: Riki
companion.desc: A lean Shikoku that Tendo did not so much train as befriend; it works scenes beside him, steady where the air goes wrong and unbothered by what bothers everyone else.
companion.role: Field companion and ward-sense: settles on safe ground, bristles and refuses to enter where the Veil is thin, buying the team a warning.

tsukishiro.cap: I recognised you before you said a word. I've been waiting three years to.
back: Thirty-one, an independent investigator who works the seam between the Grid and the official world without belonging to either. Tsukishiro Haruki is a Ritualist with a researcher's patience and a griever's persistence: for three years he has kept a private file on the pre-2011 Kita disturbances, the ones the CVD closed and he never could. He recognised something at the 2012 case where he and Gin first crossed paths, and has been quietly assembling the shape of it ever since, alone, because no institution wanted the conclusion.

He is warm in a careful way — interested in everything, cautious about everything, the two held in steady balance. Rei walks into a mystery Haruki has been half-solving for years, and Haruki has the unnerving experience of meeting the person his research has been pointing at. At depth he shares the pre-2011 file: three years of work in no record, and what he recognised at that first meeting that he has told no one.
His flaw is that solitary research has made him better at understanding people than being with them; he has theories about Rei before he has feelings, and has to learn the difference.

quest.title: Three years of a file no one wanted
quest.hook: Haruki has privately tracked the Kita disturbances since before the CVD admits they happened — and Rei is the missing piece.
stages: Earn past the cautious warmth to the researcher who takes a real risk.
Cross-reference his pre-2011 file against Gin's archive.
At depth he gives the three-year file and what he recognised in 2012.
quest.payoff: A parallel investigation that predates Rei's by years — and an ally whose careful heart is harder won than his research.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Haruki, an adult, theorises before he feels — the route is him letting the feeling outrun the theory.
beats: He understands Rei intellectually long before he risks anything emotionally.
Shared obsession is the easy intimacy; ordinary closeness is the hard one.
Reciprocation is Haruki setting the file down to actually be present.

routes.noble: He learns to be with someone, not just study them, and the loneliness finally lifts.
routes.dark: Rei becomes the most interesting case he ever worked, and never quite a person to him.
routes.tragic: The file was always pointing somewhere fatal, and loving Rei means following it to the end.

choi_hana.cap: You don't get my rank, my nodes, or my trust on day one. Try harder. Or don't.
back: Nineteen, unregistered, and running an Arbiter-grade Clairsentience she keeps deliberately invisible — because a registered Arbiter is an asset the bureaus fight over, and an unregistered one is free. Hana has survived the Grid by trusting no one quickly and testing everyone constantly; she meets Rei with open hostility, not because of who he is but because that is the only safe default she has ever had. Sharp, guarded, far more powerful than she lets anyone see.

She is the same age as Rei and lives the unregistered life he only fears — the version of him with no CVD cover, no internship, no name in any file. That makes her the most honest mirror in the campaign and the hardest contact to earn: trust from Hana is not given, it is survived to. Past the hostility she introduces Rei to Grid nodes the archive can't reach and, at the deepest tier, reveals her actual rank — the thing she has hidden from everyone, because a hidden Arbiter is a free one.
Her flaw is that armour built that young is hard to take off, even when it's safe; she tests people she's already decided to trust, just to be sure.

quest.title: The free Arbiter
quest.hook: Hana hides an Arbiter rank and a Grid that the archive can't reach — and trusts no one on day one.
stages: Survive the testing; she has decided nothing about you yet.
Earn the Grid nodes she controls, node by node.
At depth she reveals her real rank, the secret that keeps her free.
quest.payoff: Access to the unmappable Grid and an Arbiter ally — and a mirror of the unregistered life Rei is one bad day from living.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Hana, an adult of Rei's own age, lets almost no one close — the route is armour coming off in a life that punished softness.
beats: Her hostility is a test she half-hopes you'll fail so it stays simple.
Same age, opposite circumstances — she envies and resents the cover Rei has.
Intimacy is the unregistered girl risking the one thing she can't take back: trust.

routes.noble: Two nineteen-year-olds choose each other against worlds built to isolate them.
routes.dark: Rei mines her Grid and her rank and proves every reason she had not to trust.
routes.tragic: Loving a registered intern is the exposure a free Arbiter cannot survive.

kurosawa.cap: Bring me close to your brother's body. I'll tell you what's really wearing it.
back: Thirty-four, independent and Grid-adjacent, a Vanguard-grade Psychometabolist who reads bodies the way others read faces — the living, the dying, and the things wearing both. Kurosawa works the edges, taking the cases the bureaus find distasteful, because the distasteful cases are where the truth lives. He carries himself with the grim levity of a man who has touched too many corpses to be precious about death, and a sharper kindness underneath than he lets show.

He is, structurally, one of the most important people Rei can reach: get Kurosawa contact with Gin's body and he will read what no instrument can — the double-layer possession signature, how Gin surfaces, the demon's class. He is the campaign's diagnostic key to what Yushiro actually is. He also gates the path to Tanaka Ryu, whose help unlocks only through Kurosawa's trust.
His raven keeps him company on the night work; it has watched him read more bodies than either would care to count, and it knows the difference between a corpse and something pretending to be one.

quest.title: What is really wearing Gin
quest.hook: Kurosawa can read Gin's body directly — the double-layer signature, the demon's class — if Rei earns the contact.
stages: Earn the trust of a man who works the cases others won't touch.
Get him proximity to Gin's body for a true reading.
Through him, reach Tanaka Ryu and the operational fact only that track unlocks.
quest.payoff: The campaign's clearest diagnosis of Yushiro — and the gateway to Tanaka's hidden support.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Kurosawa, an adult, hides warmth under graveyard humour — the route is reaching the kindness he buries.
beats: His levity about death is armour; grief-work has cost him more than he admits.
He reads bodies but guards his own; closeness unnerves the diagnostician.
Intimacy is the man who touches the dead letting himself be touched by the living.

routes.noble: Kurosawa lets the kindness surface and stops working alone among corpses.
routes.dark: Rei uses his gift to read Gin and never sees the man behind the diagnosis.
routes.tragic: What he reads in Gin's body is also what he fears for Rei, and loving him means watching it come.

companion.name: Yoichi
companion.desc: A raven that took up with Kurosawa during a long night of body-work and never left. It sits the cold rooms with him, indifferent to the dead and intensely interested in the not-quite-dead.
companion.role: Possession-sense: unsettled and vocal near a worn body or a thing pretending to be a corpse, marking the difference Kurosawa then confirms by touch.

inoue.cap: High-threshold only. If it isn't going to end someone, don't bring it to me.
back: Twenty-seven, independent, and carrying a Singularity-grade capability so far past the ordinary scale that she has organised her whole life around not using it. Inoue takes only high-threshold cases — the ones where someone dies if she doesn't — because a power like hers cheapens into a tool the moment it's used for anything less, and she refuses to be a tool. Isolated by rank, exacting, and quietly exhausted by being the answer of last resort.

Her gift is the Null Space: she can make an operation metaphysically invisible, which is precisely what an illegal exorcism in the heart of Tokyo requires. That makes her support the difference between viable and impossible in enclosed spaces — and makes earning it a matter of proving Rei's situation is the rare thing actually worth a Singularity's attention. She reads warm from a distance and gives nothing until asked correctly.
Her flaw is the loneliness of the top of any scale: she has never met someone who needed her rather than her power, and has stopped believing she will.

quest.title: The answer of last resort
quest.hook: Inoue's Null Space can make the exorcism invisible — but she spends a Singularity only on what would otherwise kill.
stages: Prove Rei's situation clears her high threshold; she declines everything less.
Earn the woman, not the rank — she can tell the difference and is tired of people who can't.
At depth she deploys the Null Space that makes the operation viable in enclosed space.
quest.payoff: The capability that makes a hidden exorcism possible at all — and a Singularity who might, once, be needed for herself.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Inoue, an adult, is sure she'll only ever be wanted for her power — the route is being wrong about that.
beats: She braces for Rei to want the Null Space, not her; the route is him wanting her.
Singularity isolation has made closeness theoretical; she's out of practice at being a person.
Intimacy is the last resort discovering she is also a first choice.

routes.noble: Inoue is needed as herself and rejoins the human scale she'd left.
routes.dark: Rei takes the Null Space and confirms her belief that the rank is all anyone wants.
routes.tragic: The case that finally clears her threshold is the one that takes everything to win.

tanaka_ryu.cap: Kurosawa says you're alright. That buys you one showing-up. Make it count.
back: Thirty-six, independent, a field-support and stability specialist who is the person you want at your shoulder when an operation goes wrong and your own discipline starts to crack. Tanaka steadies people — that is his whole craft and most of his personality: calm, dependable, the operative who shows up without being asked and stays until it's handled. He reaches Rei only through Kurosawa, and only once Kurosawa vouches, because Tanaka's loyalty runs along trusted lines, not open ones.

He holds one operational fact about the exorcism that no one else in the campaign knows — the specific piece of intelligence that changes the approach — and it's accessible only when the Kurosawa track is fully earned. That makes him a late, decisive ally: the steady hand and the missing fact, arriving together when it matters most. Quiet, wry, more tired than he lets on.
His flaw is that he steadies everyone and lets no one steady him; he has been the reliable one so long he's forgotten he's allowed to need things.

quest.title: The steady hand and the missing fact
quest.hook: Tanaka shows up when things break — and holds the one operational fact that changes the exorcism, behind Kurosawa's trust.
stages: Earn Kurosawa first; Tanaka's loyalty runs along vouched lines only.
Prove worth the showing-up his reputation costs him.
At full trust he gives the operational fact no one else in the campaign holds.
quest.payoff: A decisive late-game ally and the single piece of intelligence that reshapes the climax.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Tanaka, an adult, steadies everyone and accepts nothing back — the route is letting himself be the one held.
beats: He shows up for Rei the way he shows up for everyone; the route is it becoming specific.
Being needed is comfortable for him; being wanted is the frightening part.
Intimacy is the steady hand admitting it shakes too.

routes.noble: Tanaka learns to lean, and the reliable man finally gets held up.
routes.dark: Rei uses the steady support and the fact, and never asks what Tanaka needs.
routes.tragic: He steadies Rei through the one operation that he himself doesn't walk out of.

majima.cap: I don't take cases that interest me anymore. Convince me yours is different.
back: Forty-one, a Grid-independent combat specialist with a Vanguard's capability and the bone-deep weariness of a man who has won too many fights to enjoy them. Majima takes the dangerous work freelance, charges when he can, and has long since stopped pretending the violence is anything but a job. Behind the gruff economy is a careful person guarding exactly one soft thing: a daughter he has told no one about, kept far from this life on purpose.

He is the muscle the climax may require — operational backup that arrives without charge once he's decided Rei is worth it, and the kind of fighter who keeps a team alive in the room where everything goes wrong. Earning him is earning past the mercenary surface to the man underneath, and at the deepest tier he tells Rei about the daughter, the secret that proves there's more keeping him careful than caution.
His dog works beside him — old, scarred, steady under the worst noise, the only colleague Majima has never had to worry about betraying him.

quest.title: The fighter with one soft thing
quest.hook: Majima is the combat backup the climax needs — and the most guarded man on the Grid.
stages: Convince him the case is worth a fight he no longer enjoys.
Earn past the mercenary surface to the careful man beneath.
At depth he trusts Rei with the daughter no one else knows exists.
quest.payoff: Vanguard-grade muscle for the operation that can't be won without it — and a guarded man's deepest secret as the measure of his trust.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Majima, an adult, has walled off softness to protect what little he has — the route is the wall coming down once.
beats: The gruffness is real and also a fence around the daughter and everything tender.
He fears that letting Rei in puts another person in range of this life.
Intimacy is the fighter deciding Rei is worth the risk he keeps everyone else from.

routes.noble: Majima lets Rei past the wall and stops carrying it all alone.
routes.dark: Rei buys the muscle and never earns the man, and the wall stays up for good reason.
routes.tragic: The life he kept his daughter from reaches the one person he let inside it.

companion.name: Tetsu
companion.desc: A grizzled, big-boned dog that has worked beside Majima for a decade — calm under gunfire and worse, scarred in places that match Majima's own.
companion.role: Combat and ward companion: holds position under chaos, refuses thin or wrong ground, and gives Majima a half-second's warning no instrument matches.

uehara.cap: Eight years I've documented them. I'm running out of time to hand it to the right person.
back: Forty-five, a former CVD Vanguard now independent and quietly deteriorating — the capability still there but flickering, a great practitioner watching his own instrument fail. For eight years Uehara has built one thing: a near-complete documentation of an organized entity campaign across the city, the pattern the bureaus refuse to see as a pattern. It lives, half of it, on a laminated page he keeps in a pocket, because paper outlasts a failing memory.

He is racing his own decline to put the work in the right hands before he can't. That makes him urgent, exacting, and unexpectedly moving: a man with little time spending it on a stranger because the stranger might finish what he can't. Once he decides Rei is that person, the laminated page comes out, and the eight-year file removes an entire tier of difficulty from the campaign's hardest act.
His flaw is pride wrestling with mortality — he wants to hand the work over and cannot quite forgive himself for needing to.

quest.title: Eight years, running out of time
quest.hook: Uehara has documented the organized entity campaign for eight years — and is failing fast enough that he needs an heir.
stages: Prove you're the right hands; he is out of time for the wrong ones.
Earn the laminated page he keeps against his own failing memory.
At depth the full eight-year file passes to Rei, removing a difficulty tier from Act 3.
quest.payoff: The single most complete intelligence on the organized campaign — and a dying master's life work entrusted to Rei.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Uehara, an adult facing decline, guards his dignity fiercely — the route is tenderness that doesn't read as pity.
beats: He cannot bear to be pitied; affection has to come as respect, not rescue.
His failing capability makes him feel like less; Rei has to want the man, not mourn him early.
Intimacy is the proud master letting himself be cared for without it diminishing him.

routes.noble: Uehara is loved as himself, not his decline, and the last years are not lonely ones.
routes.dark: Rei takes the file and lets a dying man feel used at the end.
routes.tragic: The decline wins on its own schedule, and loving him is loving someone already leaving.

mochizuki.cap: You're doing the same thing I am, aren't you. From the other side.
back: Twenty-three, unregistered, a developing Arbiter who spends her evenings in libraries assembling from the outside the same picture Rei is building from within. Mochizuki Sora is a self-taught investigator — quiet, quick, lonely in the specific way of someone who understood too much too young and had no one to tell. She recognises Rei before he finishes his first sentence, because she has been the only person in every room who sees what she sees, and suddenly there are two.

Her three years of documentation map the Kita demon's regional pattern from outside the institution — and combined with Rei's inside approach, the two investigations are structurally stronger than either alone. She is the campaign's clearest 'you are not alone in this' — a peer, an equal, a parallel that becomes a partnership. Mutual recognition is the warm start; mutual trust is the work.

Her flaw is the autodidact's wariness: she has been right and unbelieved so long that being finally understood frightens her almost as much as it relieves her. Her cat keeps the library evenings with her, the one steady presence through years of solitary work.

quest.title: The same thing, from the other side
quest.hook: Sora has mapped the Kita demon's pattern from outside for three years — the mirror of Rei's inside investigation.
stages: Meet the recognition with trust, not just relief at not being alone.
Combine her external documentation with Rei's internal access.
At depth the two investigations merge into something neither could build alone.
quest.payoff: A structurally complete picture of the Kita demon — and the campaign's truest peer, the proof Rei isn't alone.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Sora, an adult, has been understood by no one for years — the route is being finally seen and not flinching from it.
beats: Recognition is instant; trust is slow, because being believed is the unfamiliar thing.
Two people used to being the only one in the room have to learn to be two.
Intimacy is the autodidact letting someone all the way into the work and the loneliness behind it.

routes.noble: Two solitary investigators become genuine partners, in the work and out of it.
routes.dark: Rei merges her years of work into his and leaves her alone again, used.
routes.tragic: The combined investigation is right, and being right about this demon is what gets one of them killed.

companion.name: Hon
companion.desc: A library-stray cat Sora fed through three years of evening research until it simply became hers. It keeps to the reading-table lamp and dislikes exactly the people Sora later learns to dislike too.
companion.role: Quiet ward and read on people: settles by her work, bristles at residue and at bad-faith visitors, an early instinct she has learned to trust.

kaneda.cap: Sit anywhere. First drink's honest. So am I, if you are.
back: Thirty-five, bartender at The Lighthouse in Ni-chōme, civilian but quietly aware — the kind of awareness that comes from years of listening to a city's secrets across a wooden counter at two in the morning. Kaneda keeps the safest table in the district and the most honest ear; people tell him things they'd tell no one, and he keeps them the way a good bartender keeps everything: close, and only handed back to the right person.

He doesn't hunt and doesn't practise; what he offers is something rarer — a true table, a real answer, and a vouch in a quarter where vouching is everything. To Rei he is a place to breathe and a node into the nightlife's hidden traffic, and at full trust he tells him what the street really knows and speaks for him where no one speaks for strangers. Warm, watchful, unhurried.
His flaw is the bartender's occupational hazard: he has heard so many confessions he's forgotten he's allowed his own, and pours for everyone while no one pours for him.

quest.title: The honest table
quest.hook: Kaneda hears everything across his bar and vouches where no one vouches — if Rei is honest back.
stages: Be a real person at his counter, not a man working an angle.
Earn the safe table and the district knowledge that comes with it.
At full trust he tells you what the street really knows and vouches for you.
quest.payoff: A safe base in Ni-chōme, the nightlife's honest intelligence, and a vouch that opens doors strangers can't.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Kaneda, an adult, is warm to everyone — the route is being the one he's warm to off the clock.
beats: His easy warmth is genuine and also professional; the route is reaching the private man.
He hears everyone's confessions and offers none of his own.
Intimacy is the bartender finally being poured for.

routes.noble: Kaneda lets Rei past the counter to the person who's spent years listening, never heard.
routes.dark: Rei works the honest table for what it gives and gives nothing true back.
routes.tragic: What Rei brings to his door is the danger Kaneda's quiet awareness always feared.

switch.cap: The meet moves so it can't be mapped. Earn it, and you're inside. Mishandle it, and it never existed.
back: Thirty-seven, gender deliberately unfixed, the person who runs the rotating Grid meet — the Gathering that never happens twice in the same place and exists only for those vouched far enough in to find it. Switch is infrastructure: not the most powerful person in the Grid but arguably the most necessary, the hinge the whole unmappable network turns on. Careful to the point of paranoia, fair to the point of ruthlessness, and impossible to locate unless they want to be found.

For Rei, Switch is the gate to the Grid entire. Early on it's an invitation to the next Gathering; fully earned, it's being brought all the way inside — the meet, the network, the web no archive can chart. Mishandle the trust and the meet simply vanishes and the Grid is warned, and a door that took weeks to open closes for good. Switch deals in access, and access is the most valuable and most revocable currency Rei can hold.
Not a romance and not a friendship exactly — a relationship of earned access, where the warmth is real but the trust is always conditional on Rei never being a risk to the network.

quest.title: The meet that can't be mapped
quest.hook: Switch runs the rotating Grid Gathering — the gate to the whole unmappable network.
stages: Get vouched far enough in to receive an invitation at all.
Handle the first Gathering without becoming a risk to it.
At full trust, be brought fully inside the Grid — the meet, the network, the web.
quest.payoff: Access to the entire Grid — or, if mishandled, a vanished meet and a network warned against Rei.

kuroki.cap: I can find anyone in this city. The finding is free. The owing is not.
back: Fifty-one, a lieutenant in a Shinjuku family, and the most efficient locator of missing people in Tokyo precisely because his methods would horrify the bureaus he outperforms. Kuroki runs a human network the CVD and the Grid both envy and neither can replicate: doormen, drivers, landlords, the quiet economy of people who see everything and answer to the family. He is courteous, patient, and entirely without illusion about what he is.

For Rei he is a terrifying door: Kuroki can find Gin's last movements, the address in no file, the person who wants the absence kept quiet — faster than anyone. But every favour is a debt, and Kuroki's debts are paid in things Rei may not want to owe. The relationship is a slow negotiation with a man who is genuinely helpful and genuinely dangerous, and never confuses the two.
His guard dog is as much a statement as a companion — calm, enormous, and a reminder that the courtesy is a choice he is making.

quest.title: The finding is free; the owing is not
quest.hook: Kuroki's network can locate what the bureaus can't — for a debt paid in Kuroki's currency.
stages: Approach correctly; he respects form and despises desperation.
Take a small favour and learn what it costs to owe him.
Decide how deep into his debt Rei is willing to go for what only Kuroki can find.
quest.payoff: The fastest path to people and places no official channel can reach — at the price of owing organised crime.

companion.name: Banchō
companion.desc: A massive, unhurried dog that lies at Kuroki's feet like furniture until it isn't. It has never needed to do anything, which is exactly the point.
companion.role: Presence and warning: reads a room's threat before Kuroki does and tells him with a single shift of weight.

wada_sho.cap: If they knew I was talking to you, I'd be in the bay. ...I'm still talking.
back: Twenty-nine, a soldier under Kuroki, and a crack in the family wall that nobody upstairs has noticed yet. Wada took the life because it was the only one offered to a kid from where he's from, and has spent ten years discovering he doesn't have the stomach for the parts that matter. He is loyal in the way of someone who has nowhere else to be loyal, and quietly sick of it.

He becomes, at real risk to himself, the leak in the family Rei needs — a tip-off here, a looked-away there, each one a small bet against his own survival. What moves him is not money or ideology but the simple, dangerous wish to do one decent thing in a life that hasn't allowed many. Rei is the occasion for it, and that makes Rei both his hope and his exposure.
His flaw is that he mistakes recklessness for courage; he'll take a risk for Rei that's braver than it is wise, because being brave once feels worth more to him than living careful forever.

quest.title: The crack in the family wall
quest.hook: Wada will betray his own family in small, mortal increments — because he's tired of being only what they made him.
stages: Give him a reason to risk it that isn't a trap; he's watched for those.
Receive the tip-offs without getting him made.
At depth he takes a real risk that could put him in the bay — for one decent thing.
quest.payoff: Inside access to the Shinjuku family's movements — and a man betting his life on the chance to be more than a soldier.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Wada, an adult, has never been wanted for anything but his usefulness to the family — the route is being wanted as himself.
beats: He expects to be used; tenderness baffles and undoes him.
Loving Rei is the most dangerous insubordination of his life, and he knows it.
Intimacy is the soldier letting himself imagine a life past the family.

routes.noble: Wada gets out, and the one decent thing becomes a whole decent life.
routes.dark: Rei spends his loyalty like the family always did, and leaves him in the wall.
routes.tragic: The risk he takes for Rei is the one the family finally notices.

ito_kenta.cap: Pills or information, your choice. Info's cheaper and it'll actually help you.
back: Eighteen, just over the line into adulthood, and already running product for a school gang because the maths of his life never offered a better option. Itō is sharp, fast-talking, and more frightened than he'll ever show — a kid who has had to be a businessman since before he should have been, and who reads a customer's danger faster than most operatives read a room. He sells pills; he'd rather sell information, which is safer and which he's better at.

He becomes a way into the gang's real structure — its suppliers, its hierarchy, the part that matters — if Rei reaches him before the blade does. There's a version of Itō that flips on his suppliers and walks into something better, and a version that comes at Rei badly with a knife because fear won. Which one Rei meets depends on whether Rei treats him as a mark, a threat, or the first adult who saw a person.
His flaw is the survivor's reflex: he assumes every kindness is a setup, because in his experience it always has been, and he'll test Rei's the way he tests everything — by expecting it to be fake.

quest.title: Pills, or a way out
quest.hook: Itō can open the gang's real structure — if Rei reaches the kid before the life closes over him.
stages: Be the kindness that isn't a setup; he's testing for the trick.
Buy information instead of leaving him to sell pills.
At depth he flips on his suppliers — a way in, and a way out for him.
quest.payoff: Access to the gang's supply chain and hierarchy — and a frightened kid who might get to be more than a dealer.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Itō is just eighteen and an adult, but raw — the route is gentle, earned, and about safety as much as feeling.
beats: He's been a businessman so long that being cared for reads as a con to him.
Trust comes hard and late; he flinches toward the exit on instinct.
Intimacy is the kid who sells to survive letting himself simply be eighteen.

routes.noble: Itō gets out and learns, slowly, that the kindness was real.
routes.dark: Rei works him like every adult before, and the blade-version wins.
routes.tragic: He flips for Rei, and the suppliers find out who talked.

aizawa_yuto.cap: My family has money for everything except the thing I actually need. Funny, right?
back: Twenty-two, heir to a name that has given him everything except a reason, and addicted in the slow, well-funded way of someone whose every comfort is a way of not feeling the emptiness underneath. Yuto is charming, generous, self-destructive, and far smarter than the dissipation suggests — he sees exactly what he's doing and can't, on his own, find the handle to stop. The nightlife knows him as the easy round and the soft touch; almost no one knows the boy underneath is drowning on purpose because sinking is quieter than asking for help.

He becomes, at the deepest point, a choice with two endings: the version where he reaches his family and asks, once, sober, for help — a rescue — and the version where he doesn't, and Rei is left holding the after. Rei is, for Yuto, the rare person who likes him without wanting anything from the name, which is the first foothold he's had in years.
His flaw is the addict's: he will choose the anesthetic over the person every time it's offered, right up until the moment, if it comes, that he doesn't.

quest.title: The one sober ask
quest.hook: Yuto is drowning in funded comfort — and Rei might be the foothold that gets him to ask for help, once, sober.
stages: Like him for himself, not the name or the easy rounds.
Be steady through the relapses without becoming his enabler or his savior.
At depth he reaches his family and asks, sober, for help — a rescue or a tragedy.
quest.payoff: A wealthy, well-connected ally pulled back from the edge — or the grief of holding the after when the ask never comes.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Yuto, an adult, confuses being wanted with being used — the route is care that doesn't enable and doesn't rescue.
beats: He offers the easy version of himself; the route is reaching the one that's drowning.
Loving him is not the same as fixing him, and Rei has to know the difference.
Intimacy is Yuto choosing, once, the person over the anesthetic.

routes.noble: Yuto gets sober for himself, and Rei is the one who liked him enough to wait.
routes.dark: Rei takes the easy rounds and the soft touch and lets the boy keep drowning.
routes.tragic: The anesthetic wins the last time it's offered, and Rei holds the after.

leo_sato.cap: The rich tell their hosts everything. I remember all of it. Be nice to me.
back: Twenty-six, a Kabukichō host with a clairsentient medium's read that he uses, professionally, to make every client feel like the only person in the world. 'Leo' is the working name; Sato is the man, and the gap between them is the whole performance — warmth dispensed by the hour, intimacy as a service, and underneath it a sharp, watchful intelligence cataloguing every secret the powerful let slip when they think they're being adored.

That cataloguing is what makes him valuable: the rich confess to their hosts, and Leo remembers all of it. He trades a client's dangerous secret for the right consideration — the kind of leverage no investigator could otherwise touch. To Rei he performs friendship effortlessly and means none of it at first, because meaning it is the one thing he never does on the clock. Earning the man behind Leo means being the rare person who doesn't want to be performed at.
His exotic little companion is part of the act and part of the truth — a host's beautiful accessory, and the one creature he doesn't have to perform for.

quest.title: The rich confess to their hosts
quest.hook: Leo remembers every secret the powerful let slip while being adored — and trades them for the right consideration.
stages: See past the performance to the man cataloguing the room.
Earn a client's dangerous secret without becoming a mark yourself.
At depth he hands Rei leverage no investigator could otherwise reach.
quest.payoff: Access to the confessions of Tokyo's powerful — and, if earned, the real person behind the working name.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Leo, an adult, performs intimacy for a living — the route is the one person he stops performing for.
beats: He gives flawless manufactured warmth; the route is reaching the unmanufactured kind.
He fears he's only the performance, and that there's no Sato left under Leo.
Intimacy is the host being adored without having to earn it by the hour.

routes.noble: Leo finds Sato again, and gives Rei the warmth he never sells.
routes.dark: Rei buys the performance and the secrets and never meets the man.
routes.tragic: A client's secret is the wrong one to have traded, and it comes back for them both.

companion.name: Suzu
companion.desc: A slow, beautiful snake Leo keeps as part of the act and loves off it — the one creature in his life he never has to charm, because it asks nothing and remembers nothing.
companion.role: Read on a visitor: unusually restless in the presence of veil-residue or a worn body, a quiet tell Leo has learned to watch.

mali.cap: Strong hands, sharper eyes. I know who's lying on my table before they do.
back: Twenty-eight, a lady-boy working a Thai parlour near the Peony — real bodywork, a blunt mouth the regulars come back for, and the best informal read on Ōkubo's hidden community that anyone outside it will ever get. Mali has strong hands and stronger eyes; people relax on her table and tell her things, and she forgets none of it. She is fiercely loving with her people and entirely out of patience with anyone who disrespects them.

For Rei she is a door into the Thai community and the strip's workers — eyes in the places the CVD will never be welcome and the Grid never thinks to look. What she offers is an honest read on who in the quarter is hiding and who is hunting, and at full trust she opens the whole network of workers who watch the street better than any operative. She gives it only to someone who treats her people as people.
Her flaw is the protector's: she has built a wall around her own and will test Rei hard at the door, because everyone who ever wanted in before wanted to take something out.

quest.title: Eyes the CVD will never have
quest.hook: Mali reads Ōkubo's hidden community better than any bureau — and guards it like family.
stages: Prove you treat her people as people, not as informants.
Earn the honest read on who's hiding and who's hunting in the quarter.
At full trust she opens the Thai community and the strip's workers to you.
quest.payoff: Eyes across Ōkubo and the workers' network — the surveillance the CVD and Grid both lack, given only on respect.

romance.opens: Player chooses it; Mali, an adult, has been wanted for what she knows and not who she is — the route is being chosen for herself.
beats: Her bluntness is a gate; warmth is what she guards behind it.
She tests hard because everyone before wanted to take something from her people.
Intimacy is the protector letting herself be the one looked after.

routes.noble: Mali is loved as herself, and lets Rei all the way inside the wall.
routes.dark: Rei mines the network and proves she was right to guard the door.
routes.tragic: What Rei brings to Ōkubo is the danger she built the wall against.

companion.name: Nong
companion.desc: A parlour cat that owns the front room and tolerates the clients. Mali feeds it scraps and talks to it like a colleague; it likes exactly three regulars and is right about all three.
companion.role: Read on a visitor and a calm in the room: settles the nervous, bristles at the wrong ones, an instinct Mali trusts over her own.

mariko.cap: The cells take the lost ones. Sometimes I get to them first. Sometimes.
back: Forties, a worker at the Peony Rooms in Uguisudani, and quietly one of the few people standing between a lost, unregistered medium and the institutions that would disappear them. 'Mariko' is a working name worn by a woman who has seen the fallen network up close — the sensitives who slipped through every crack, ended up in the rooms, and have no one official who will help without filing them. She does what she can, which is more than anyone asks of her.

For Rei she is a rescuer with a weight: she can bring him a lost, unregistered medium before the cells do — a person saved, and a responsibility handed over. She knows who has passed through the quarter and what became of them, and shares it only with someone she trusts not to be another kind of cell. She is wary by reflex and warmer than the wariness suggests.

Her flaw is that she carries more than one person can, and has learned to expect that anyone offering to help is really there to take — so she watches Rei a long time before she decides he's the rare exception.

quest.title: Before the cells get them
quest.hook: Mariko reaches lost, unregistered mediums before the institutions do — and might hand one to Rei.
stages: Prove you're not just another kind of cell.
Earn the quiet record of who's passed through the quarter.
At depth she brings Rei a lost medium before the cells do — a rescue and a weight.
quest.payoff: A pipeline to the fallen network the bureaus erase — and the responsibility that comes with every soul she hands over.

endo_masa.cap: I decide who comes through this door. You behave, you're in.
back: Thirty-eight, doorman at Vault in Roppongi, low-sensitive in a way he's never named but has always trusted — the 'gut thing' that tells him which guest is trouble before they reach the rope. Endō is the gate to a corner of the nightlife, and the gate is a position of real, quiet power: he sees everyone who comes and goes, remembers faces, and owes loyalty to no one but the door.

For Rei he is a safe door, a lost tail, a walk to the taxi when the night turns wrong — and, at full trust, an early-warning net across the nightlife wards, his gut thing tuned to exactly the wrongness Rei hunts. He gives it slowly, because a doorman who trusts too easily isn't a doorman for long. Respect the door and the door opens; disrespect it and Roppongi closes a row of doors at once.
